articles.title: How to Job Hunt Effectively in Australia
articles.excerpt: A step-by-step guide to finding the right role faster, from tailoring your resume to nailing the follow-up.
articles.author: Emma Wilson
content: Job hunting in Australia has changed dramatically over the last few years. Employers now expect tailored applications, and the hidden job market accounts for a large share of hires.
Start by clarifying what you actually want. Write down three must-haves and three deal-breakers. This filter saves hours of applying for roles that aren't a fit.
Next, tailor your resume for each role. Mirror the language in the job ad, especially the key skills listed in the first paragraph.
Finally, follow up. A polite email a week after applying often surfaces opportunities that were otherwise overlooked.

articles.title: 10 Resume Tips That Actually Get Interviews
articles.excerpt: Recruiters spend 6–8 seconds on the first scan. Here's how to make every one of them count.
articles.author: Daniel Lee
content: Keep it to two pages unless you're an academic. Recruiters value clarity over completeness.
Lead with an impact summary, not an objective statement. 'Marketing leader who grew revenue 40% YoY' beats 'Seeking a challenging role'.
Use ATS-friendly formatting: standard headings, no tables, no columns.

articles.title: The 15 Most Common Interview Questions (and How to Answer)
articles.excerpt: Prepare once, walk in confident. These are the questions 90% of Australian interviewers ask.
articles.author: Priya Sharma
content: Tell me about yourself. Two minutes max: current role, one career highlight, why this job.
Why do you want to work here? Reference something specific about the company — not just 'great culture'.
What's your biggest weakness? Pick a real one and show the corrective action.

articles.title: How to Negotiate Your Salary Confidently
articles.excerpt: Most candidates leave money on the table. Here's a calm, evidence-based script that works.
articles.author: Michael O'Brien
content: Never give the first number. Ask: 'What range has been budgeted for this role?'
Anchor with market data. SEEK, Hays, and Robert Half publish free salary guides.
Negotiate the package, not just the base — super, WFH days, and training budgets count.

articles.title: Changing Careers at Any Age
articles.excerpt: You're never too old to pivot. A practical roadmap for a career change in Australia.
articles.author: Emily Watson
content: Audit your transferable skills. Most career changers underestimate what already counts.
Test the new field with a side project, volunteering, or a short course before you leap.
Rebuild your network. Informational interviews open more doors than applications.

articles.title: Remote Work Rights in Australia: What You Need to Know
articles.excerpt: WFH isn't just a perk — it's increasingly protected. Here's what the law says.
articles.author: Sophia Nguyen
content: The Fair Work Act now includes a right to request flexible arrangements for many employees.
Employers can refuse on reasonable business grounds — but they must respond in writing.
Keep records of your requests and responses.

articles.title: Visa Sponsorship Explained for Job Seekers
articles.excerpt: Which Australian visas allow sponsorship, and how to spot employers who actually offer it.
articles.author: David Kumar
content: The TSS 482 visa is the most common temporary sponsored visa.
Employers must be approved sponsors — check the Home Affairs sponsor list.
Ask recruiters directly: 'Does this role come with visa sponsorship?'

articles.title: Upskilling for the Future of Work
articles.excerpt: The skills Australian employers will pay a premium for in 2025 and beyond.
articles.author: Olivia Brown
content: AI literacy is quickly becoming baseline, not bonus.
Soft skills — communication, adaptability, judgment — are the hardest to automate.
Micro-credentials from TAFE and universities are a fast, affordable route.
